input: Sort out travel visa for Japan trip

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Visa requirements differ significantly based on the applicant's nationality — some countries have visa-free access to Japan, making the task trivial, while others require a full application process.
The type of visa needed (tourist, business, work, student) determines entirely different forms, documents, and processes.
The intended travel date sets the urgency of the task and determines whether standard or express processing is needed.
Whether the user has already gathered supporting documents (passport, bank statements, itinerary, etc.) determines how much groundwork remains.
Knowing whether to apply through an embassy, consulate, or a visa agency changes the specific steps and submission method involved.
Understanding whether 'sort out' means just researching requirements vs. fully submitting the application defines where the finish line is.
If travelling with others (family, group), a joint or accompanying application process may be needed, changing the scope and workload.

gold.taskTitle: Sort out Japan travel visa application
gold.taskDescription: The user needs to research, prepare, and apply for a visa to travel to Japan.

questions.title: What is your current nationality or passport country?
questions.description: The applicant's passport nationality determines whether a visa is even required for Japan, and if so, what type of application process applies.

questions.title: What type of visit to Japan are you planning?
questions.description: Identifies whether the trip is for tourism, business, study, or work — each requiring a different visa category with distinct forms and supporting documents.

questions.title: When are you planning to travel to Japan?
questions.description: The intended departure date determines the urgency of the application and whether standard or expedited processing is needed.

questions.title: Which supporting documents do you already have ready?
questions.description: Establishing what documents (passport, bank statements, flight itinerary, accommodation) are already prepared shows how much work remains before submission.

questions.title: Will you apply directly or use a visa agency?
questions.description: Determines the submission route — embassy/consulate in person, by post, or via a third-party visa service — which changes the specific steps and timeline.

questions.title: Does 'sort out' mean fully submitted, or just researched and ready?
questions.description: Clarifies where the user considers the task complete — at the research stage, document preparation stage, or actual submission of the application.

questions.title: Are you applying alone or with other travellers?
questions.description: If travelling with family members or a group, additional or joint applications may be needed, expanding the overall scope and effort of the task.
